subject: RFP: Security acceptance packet — assembly instructions and sample exports
messages:
From: Elizabeth White <elizabeth.white@northridge.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.inference>
Cc: procurement@northridge.com, Sam Park <sam@sigmaassess.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial asset request — RFP Section 5.2 (SOC 2 / ISO / SIG)

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for engaging on the Northridge RFP. Section 5.2 of our procurement packet asks for a "Security acceptance packet" containing the following: a redacted SOC 2 Type II report, current ISO 27001 certificate, a completed SIG questionnaire (or subset) with control references, a control-to-RFP mapping (CSV preferred), and a small set of supporting artifacts (audit log excerpt, key management diagram, retention policy excerpt).

Can you confirm whether Redwood can produce these items, and provide an expected delivery window? Our timeline is tight — packet due to the evaluation committee by 2027-09-30. If any artifact requires an NDA or additional redaction, please flag it and propose an alternate.

Also: is there a specific assembly format you prefer (single ZIP, per-document PDFs, a table of contents)? We aim to consume the packet programmatically, so a structured map/CSV will help.

Appreciate a quick note on what you can deliver and any blockers.

Best,
Elizabeth White
Procurement Manager
Northridge Financial

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.inference>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>
Cc: (internal)
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Initial asset request — RFP Section 5.2 (SOC 2 / ISO / SIG)

Team — forwarding Northridge's ask. Packet due 2027-09-30 to evaluation committee; customer prefers a CSV mapping and a program-friendly structure. Can we commit to a deliverable set and owners? My suggested split below — please confirm.

Suggested owners / outputs:
- Karthik: control map (CSV) + KMS + audit log excerpt (technical artifacts) — deliver by 2027-09-27.
- Neha: SIG subset + redacted SOC2 Type II (legal/redaction) — deliver by 2027-09-26.
- Ben: packet assembly instructions (TOC, ZIP layout) + final packaging & file naming — deliver by 2027-09-28.

Blockers to flag: any legal redaction on SOC 2 or customer-sensitive logs, and whether Procurement requires DocuSign for an NDA addendum before we share audit logs. Elizabeth asked about preferred format; let's propose: single ZIP with a top-level index.csv mapping each artifact to RFP control IDs, and a small README (packet_assembly_instructions_v1.md).

Please reply with any objections or changes to owners/times.

Thanks,
Tessa
Head of Customer Success
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.inference>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Initial asset request — RFP Section 5.2 (SOC 2 / ISO / SIG)

On Tue, Sep 14, 2027 at 11:05 AM Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.inference> wrote:
> Team — forwarding Northridge's ask...

We can produce the requested artifacts with a few clarifications. Quick summary of what I can ship and caveats: 

1) Control map (CSV): I will produce a CSV that maps RFP control IDs -> our internal control IDs -> evidence filename. Will include columns: rfp_control_id, redwood_control_id, evidence_file, evidence_type, redaction_required (yes/no).

2) KMS / key diagram: we can provide a PDF diagram and a short narrative describing envelope encryption and HSM integrations. Be explicit that customer-managed keys are an add-on for Private deployments.

3) Audit log excerpt: we will provide a redacted S3/auditlog tail (timestamps truncated to day-level, user ids hashed) — this will be a .txt artifact. We need an NDA before shipping raw logs; otherwise provide a synthesized sample that mirrors structure but is synthetic. 

4) SOC 2 Type II: we can provide a redacted copy (service descriptions and customer names removed). Legal will review for PII.

5) SIG: completing a full SIG (1000+ Qs) is heavy — propose a filled subset (security-critical controls) + the full SIG answer index with links to our public docs and referenced artifacts in the ZIP.

6) ISO27001 certificate: we can include the PDF of current certificate.

Ben, I'll drop preliminary files into a working Drive folder and include a short packet_assembly_instructions_v1.md that lists expected ZIP layout. Please confirm packaging preferences — programmatic index.csv is fine.

Deliverables timeline (firming up): draft CSV + diagrams by 2027-09-24, artifacts for legal review by 2027-09-26, final ZIP to customer by 2027-09-29 (one day buffer). If Procurement insists on DocuSign NDA for logs, we will shift logs to synthetic sample and include instructions to request NDA.

-Karthik
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Elizabeth White <elizabeth.white@northridge.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.inference>
Cc: Sam Park <sam@sigmaassess.com>, procurement@northridge.com
Date: Mon, 27 Sep 2027 08:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP: Security acceptance packet — assembly instructions and sample exports

Tessa,

Thanks — that timeline works for us. A couple quick clarifications from the evaluation committee: 

- The committee prefers real audit excerpts where possible; if an NDA is needed for raw logs, a synthetic sample is acceptable but please annotate the CSV mapping to indicate which artifacts are synthetic.
- For the SIG, the committee needs the control-level answers for our top 60 security controls — the subset approach is acceptable as long as it is clearly labelled.
- Please include a network/architecture stack diagram showing tenant isolation for your hosted product and separation of customer data when using Dedicated and Private deployments.

Also, we can expedite a minimal NDA (two-way) — procurement@northridge.com copied here. If you can send a DocuSign stub we will route internally; signature would speed log shipment.

One more ask: please include a short index file listing redactions applied to each artifact (redaction_manifest.csv or similar).

If you can confirm by end of day 2027-09-27 we'll put you on the review queue for 2027-09-29.

Best,
Elizabeth

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.inference>
To: Elizabeth White <elizabeth.white@northridge.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>, procurement@northridge.com, Sam Park <sam@sigmaassess.com>
Date: Sat, 02 Oct 2027 16:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Final packet delivery + next steps (Northridge RFP)

Elizabeth / team —

Attached is our submission package for the RFP security acceptance packet. Per the committee's ask, we included: 

- redwood_control_map_RFP_Northridge_v1.xlsx (control mapping CSV exported as XLSX)
- sig_q_responses_excerpt.pdf (control-level answers for Northridge top 60 controls)
- s3_audit_log_sample_20270927.txt (synthetic redacted audit tail; logs require two-way NDA for raw export)
- iso27001_certificate_current.pdf (official certificate)
- packet_assembly_instructions_v1.md (README + expected ZIP layout and naming conventions)
- redaction_manifest.csv (clear mapping of what was redacted and why)

Notes and caveats: 
- The audit text file is synthetic to avoid sharing identifiable user IDs; we have included an annotated redaction_manifest.csv that explains transformations. If Procurement executes the two-way NDA (DocuSign link below), Karthik will provide an expanded raw extract under agreed limits.
- The SIG excerpt contains direct references to evidence files inside the ZIP; full SIG is available on request but is heavy — we provided the indexed pointer to the full SIG hosted in our secure assessment portal.
- The control map CSV follows the format Karthik outlined (rfp_control_id, redwood_control_id, evidence_file, evidence_type, redaction_required).

DocuSign: https://docusign.net/stub/NORT-ndax-2027-09 (please route to procurement@northridge.com)

Next steps I propose: 
1) Confirm receipt and whether the synthetic audit tail is acceptable for initial review.
2) If Procurement signs NDA, we'll push the raw audit tail package within 48 hours of signature and note the change in redaction_manifest.csv.
3) If reviewers request additional artifacts (more logs, KMS key rotation schedule), flag them and we will treat as an addendum.

If you want a short handoff call to walk through the ZIP and answer control mapping questions, Karthik and I are available next week; propose 2027-10-05 09:00–09:30 PT.

Thanks for the partnership — good luck with the committee review.

Regards,

Tessa Morgan
Head of Customer Success
Redwood Inference
+t: +1 (415) 555-0123
https://redwood.inference/docs/security

Attachments: redwood_control_map_RFP_Northridge_v1.xlsx (xlsx), s3_audit_log_sample_20270927.txt (text), sig_q_responses_excerpt.pdf (pdf), packet_assembly_instructions_v1.md (md), redaction_manifest.csv (csv)
